concepts.label: circuit
concepts.gloss: A circuit is an end-to-end transport connection presented at defined hand-off demarcation points and carried across an underlying bearer.
concepts.example: CIR-7 provides transport between the NY and FRA hand-offs and is carried on the 193.1 THz NY–FRA wavelength.

concepts.label: hand-off
concepts.gloss: A hand-off is a circuit-specific demarcation point at which an endpoint of a transport circuit is presented to an adjoining customer or network system.
concepts.example: ho-NY-CIR7 is the New York presentation point of CIR-7, while ho-FRA-CIR7 is its Frankfurt presentation point.

concepts.label: rate
concepts.gloss: A rate is the specified transport capacity or throughput commitment associated with a circuit.
concepts.example: CIR-7 has a committed rate of 5 Gbit/s between its NY and FRA hand-offs.

concepts.label: latency
concepts.gloss: Latency is the measured or specified transport delay for a circuit, potentially qualified by the path on which the delay applies.
concepts.example: The primary path of CIR-7 has a recorded latency of 7.2 ms.

concepts.label: protection
concepts.gloss: Protection is the redundancy and failover arrangement assigned to a circuit to preserve transport service when a path or resource fails.
concepts.example: CIR-7 uses 1+1 path protection, with traffic protected by two concurrently provisioned paths.

concepts.label: grade
concepts.gloss: A grade is the service-quality tier assigned to a transport circuit, distinguishing levels such as premium, standard, or unguaranteed treatment.
concepts.example: CIR-7 is assigned the platinum grade rather than gold or best-effort service.

concepts.label: bearer
concepts.gloss: A bearer is an underlying transport channel, such as an optical wavelength, that carries one or more circuits across the network.
concepts.example: The bearer identified as lambda 193.1 THz NY–FRA carries CIR-7 between New York and Frankfurt.
